name: TOPY.AI AI CPO skills
description: AI CPO skills for founders, built for TOPY.AI: a chief product officer that decides what to build and proves it worked — feedback triaged with clear accept/reject rules, de-identified user research, a PMF survey, RICE priorities, a now/next/later roadmap, PRDs with a success metric, a build-or-not check before the AI CTO, pre-registered experiments read without peeking, and a decision log with falsifiers — on the TOPY CPO MCP server (https://topy.ai/mcp/cpo); standalone skills are product methods that work anywhere.

tiers.core: Runs on the TOPY MCP server; needs a TOPY account.
tiers.connected: Uses TOPY data and actions when the MCP server is connected; works on its own otherwise.
tiers.standalone: A product method that works with any agent; can use TOPY where it fits.

skills.name: Connect the AI CPO
skills.summary: Connect the TOPY CPO MCP server and check what it can see: the product review, the feedback queue, experiments and the decision log.

skills.name: Daily product watch
skills.summary: Weekdays: new feedback to triage, experiments due for a read-out and decisions due for revisit — a note to the Founder only when something needs attention.

skills.name: The CPO's goals
skills.summary: The AI CPO's standing goals and its status report for the CEO: activation, weekly active users and the PMF score, each with source and date or 'no data'.

skills.name: Weekly product review
skills.summary: Every Tuesday: usage, the feedback queue by theme, experiments due for a read-out and decisions due for revisit, with at most three actions — for the Founder and the CEO.

skills.name: Capture feedback
skills.summary: Record a piece of user feedback — a bug, an idea, praise or a question — with where it came from, de-identified, so triage can act on it.

skills.name: Close the loop
skills.summary: Draft the reply each sender is owed — fixed, coming, not planned and why, or one precise question — in plain words and their language, for the Founder to send.

skills.name: Triage feedback
skills.summary: Decide each new item — accept, reject, duplicate or needs info — size it small, medium or large, and route it: small and safe to the AI CTO, larger or sensitive ones to a PRD and the Founder.

skills.name: PMF survey
skills.summary: Run the product/market-fit survey properly — the 'very disappointed' question to the right users, 40% as the signal — and read who the product is a must-have for.

skills.name: Positioning and competitor teardown
skills.summary: Write the positioning — for whom, what job, which category, what benefit, unlike which alternative — from a sourced teardown of the real alternatives.

skills.name: User research
skills.summary: Plan and run a small round of user interviews about past behaviour, then turn the notes into de-identified insights and recorded feedback.

skills.name: Build or not
skills.summary: Before the AI CTO writes code: reuse what exists, compose a routine for a one-off, or build — privately or as a reusable app — with the reason recorded.

skills.name: Write a PRD
skills.summary: Write a one-page PRD — problem, evidence, goals, non-goals, success metric and how it is measured, risks, rollout, open questions — that the AI CTO can build from.

skills.name: RICE prioritisation
skills.summary: Rank candidate features by RICE — reach × impact × confidence ÷ effort — with the scales written down, so the order is explainable and the decision stays a person's.

skills.name: Roadmap: now, next, later
skills.summary: Keep one roadmap in three stages — now (committed), next (shaped), later (ideas) — ordered by value and effort, tied to goals, with no fake dates.

skills.name: Plan and start an experiment
skills.summary: Pre-register an A/B test — hypothesis, one primary metric, minimum detectable effect, sample size, duration and stop rule — then start it.

skills.name: Read an experiment honestly
skills.summary: Read a test against its pre-registered plan: keep running until the sample is reached, check the split, report the effect with its uncertainty and guardrails, and log the decision.

skills.name: Instrument and ship behind a flag
skills.summary: Before launch: define and verify the events the success metric needs, ship behind a feature flag to a small share first, watch guardrails, and keep a one-switch rollback.

skills.name: Log a decision
skills.summary: Record a product decision with why, the evidence and a falsifier — what would change it — and a date to revisit, so decisions can be checked instead of re-argued.

skills.name: Revisit decisions
skills.summary: When a decision's revisit date comes, check its falsifier against what the tools now show, and keep it, change it or extend the date — with a new log entry.
